connections.why: The Conquest imposed the feudal system that shaped medieval society and economy
The power of the Church behind the Crusades fed its struggle with the Crown
Conflict over royal power drove the concessions of Magna Carta
The plague struck a feudal society and shattered its labour and economy
Labour shortages and discontent after the plague helped trigger the revolt
Long-running disputes over royal versus parliamentary power culminated in civil war
Henry VIII's break with Rome set up the religious tensions Elizabeth had to settle
The European Reformation provided the ideas behind England's own break with Rome
Victory in the civil wars led to the republican Interregnum
The failure of the republic brought about the Restoration of the monarchy
The Glorious Revolution settlement shaped the Union and the Jacobite challenges to it
Parliament's growing power after 1688 underpins the later struggle over the franchise
Early colonies and contact with India were the seeds of the later British Empire
Enlightenment scientific thinking laid the ground for Darwin's theory
Enlightenment ideas about liberty and government inspired the American Revolution
Industrial power and demand for resources and markets drove imperial expansion
The slave trade was central to the wealth and growth of the empire
Industrial society created the new classes that demanded political reform
The empire built in the 19th century was dismantled in the 20th
The unresolved Irish question carried into the era of the First World War
The war's settlement shaped the instability and depression of the inter-war years
The Depression and rise of dictators led directly to the Second World War
The Holocaust was carried out under cover of the Second World War
Wartime experience built the consensus behind the post-war welfare state
The war reshaped Britain's diminished place in the post-war world
